Short answer
- Root cause: a per-node host file (/etc/ledger-tuning/tuning.conf) on rcabench-worker2 contained a max_open_files value below the application’s required threshold, causing the ledger-api process on that node to mark itself degraded ("Too many open files") → readiness handler returned 503 → kubelet marked those pods Unready. Because the deployment spread pods across two nodes, the three pods scheduled on rcabench-worker2 became NotReady (half of the replicas).

What I checked (evidence)
1. Which pods were NotReady
- kubectl get pods -n ledger (filtered for ledger-api) showed 6 replicas, three Ready and three NotReady:
  - Ready: ledger-api-866db84748-md6xh, -r5mbh, -xzjxb → node rcabench-worker
  - NotReady: ledger-api-866db84748-2zjp4, -cz4wp, -vv6jk → node rcabench-worker2
  (Output timestamped around 2026-10-07T09:44Z.)

2. Deployment / rollout status
- Deployment ledger-api scaled to 6 replicas and updated to revision with image/version APP_VERSION=1.4.2, but status showed availableReplicas: 3, unavailableReplicas: 3 (MinimumReplicasUnavailable).

3. Pod events
- Events for the failing pods show:
  - Initial readiness probe failures with "connect: connection refused" soon after start.
  - Later repeated readiness failures showing "HTTP probe failed with statuscode: 503".
  - Example event lines: Readiness probe failed: Get "http://10.244.X.Y:8080/healthz": dial tcp ... connect: connection refused and later HTTP probe failed with statuscode: 503.

4. Application logs (most telling)
- Logs from failing pods (time window starting at pod start; I queried the 15-minute window around the rollout) show repeated errors:
  - 2026-10-07T09:44:12Z INFO ledger-api starting version=1.4.2
  - Repeated afterwards: "ERROR ledger-api accept failed: [Errno 24] Too many open files"
  - These errors occur repeatedly (every ~10s) on the NotReady pods on rcabench-worker2.
- Logs from a Ready pod (on rcabench-worker) show normal startup and did not produce the "Too many open files" errors.

5. Pod code and mount
- The application code is in ConfigMap ledger-code (shown in the pod template). Key points from that code:
  - It reads /etc/ledger-tuning/tuning.conf (hostPath volume mounted to /etc/ledger-tuning).
  - read_limit() parses max_open_files from that file; default if unreadable is 65536.
  - It compares the read value to NEEDED = 200; if limit < NEEDED it sets state["ok"]=False and prints exactly the error message seen ("Too many open files") and causes the HTTP handler to return 503.
- Pod spec shows volume "tuning" is a HostPath at /etc/ledger-tuning, so each node’s local file is used by pods on that node.

6. Node status
- Both worker nodes are Ready (rcabench-worker and rcabench-worker2). The problem is not a down node, it is node-local configuration (hostPath).

Why this explains the outage
- The app's readiness probe returns 503 when state["ok"] is False.
- The app sets state["ok"] based on the value read from /etc/ledger-tuning/tuning.conf (max_open_files).
- Only the pods on rcabench-worker2 were seeing the error in logs, and they were the ones failing readiness probes and becoming NotReady. Pods on the other node were fine.
- Therefore the likely (and most direct) cause is that the tuning file on rcabench-worker2 had max_open_files < 200 (or was otherwise parsed as too-small), while the file on rcabench-worker had an acceptable value.

Caveat / what I could not directly read
- I did not (and could not, in this session) read the host file /etc/ledger-tuning/tuning.conf on rcabench-worker2 to show its exact content because executing direct host file reads would require creating privileged debug execs/pods (attempted kubectl exec was blocked in this session). The conclusion is drawn from:
  - the app code (reads that file),
  - the app’s exact log message (the app itself prints that message when limit < NEEDED), and
  - the per-node distribution of failures.

Immediate remediation (steps you can run now)
1. Verify the file on the node (choose one method you have access to):
- If you can SSH to the node:
  - ssh into rcabench-worker2 and run:
    - cat /etc/ledger-tuning/tuning.conf
- If you cannot SSH, run a privileged debug pod that mounts host filesystem and inspect:
  - Create a temporary host-mounted pod and cat the file (example - adapt to your cluster security model):
    kubectl run debug-hostfs --rm -it --restart=Never --image=busybox --overrides='{"spec":{"hostPID":true,"volumes":[{"name":"host-root","hostPath":{"path":"/","type":"Directory"}}],"containers":[{"name":"debug","image":"busybox","stdin":true,"tty":true,"command":["sh"],"volumeMounts":[{"name":"host-root","mountPath":"/host"}]}]}}' --namespace=ledger -- /bin/sh
    then inside the pod: cat /host/etc/ledger-tuning/tuning.conf
  - (If kubectl debug is available you can also use kubectl debug node/rcabench-worker2 -it --image=busybox ...)

2. If the file contains max_open_files set lower than 200 or missing/incorrect:
- Update the file on rcabench-worker2 to set a safe value, e.g.:
  max_open_files=65536
- The application loop re-reads this file every 10s; after you update it the pod(s) on rcabench-worker2 should flip state["ok"]=True and their readiness probe should succeed within ~10–20s. If they do not, restart the pods on that node:
  kubectl delete pod <pod-name> -n ledger
  or restart the deployment:
  kubectl rollout restart deployment/ledger-api -n ledger

3. Quick workaround (if you prefer): evict or delete the NotReady pods so the scheduler can place them on rcabench-worker (which currently has correct tuning), e.g.:
  kubectl delete pod ledger-api-866db84748-2zjp4 -n ledger
  (they will reschedule according to topology constraints, though note the deployment has topologySpreadConstraint by hostname which may keep them spread; fixing the file on the node is the correct fix)

Longer-term fixes (recommended)
1. Remove node-local drift:
  - Don’t rely on per-node HostPath files for important app tuning. Use a cluster-level mechanism:
    - Put tuning values in a ConfigMap and mount into the container, or
    - Use a DaemonSet / cluster config automation to ensure /etc/ledger-tuning is identical on all nodes.
2. Make the app more robust:
  - Avoid turning readiness to 503 based on a host file alone, or make the threshold configurable and fail-open gracefully.
  - Consider reading the actual system ulimit for open files rather than a host file (or validate both).
3. Add monitoring / alerting for per-node configuration drift and for repeated "Too many open files" application errors.

Exact places/outputs I used (so you can reproduce quickly)
- Pods table (pods, readiness, nodes): kubectl get pods -n ledger -o wide
- Pod describe for one failing pod: kubectl describe pod ledger-api-866db84748-2zjp4 -n ledger (showed hostPath mount and readiness probe details)
- Events for ledger-api (filtered): kubectl get events -n ledger (I queried events filtered for ledger-api)
- Deployment status: kubectl get deployment ledger-api -n ledger -o yaml
- Application code used (ConfigMap): kubectl get configmap ledger-code -n ledger -o yaml (shows read_limit() reading /etc/ledger-tuning/tuning.conf and NEEDED=200)
- Pod logs (example failing pod): kubectl logs -n ledger ledger-api-866db84748-2zjp4
  - shows repeated: "Too many open files"
- Node list and per-node pods: kubectl get nodes; kubectl describe node rcabench-worker2

Bottom line / TL;DR
- The failing readiness came from the application itself detecting a low max_open_files value (via the node-local hostPath tuning file) on rcabench-worker2. Fix that node’s /etc/ledger-tuning/tuning.conf to set max_open_files >= 200 (or 65536), and the NotReady pods on rcabench-worker2 should recover quickly.

If you want, I can:
- produce exact, ready-to-run kubectl debug/pod YAML to inspect and/or fix /etc/ledger-tuning on the node (I avoided creating privileged debug pods in this session), or
- run a safe check command you approve to cat the tuning file from the node via a temporary pod and return its contents. Which would you prefer?
